newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian plane makers strike, block road with jet.
newsitem.headline: Romanian plane makers strike, block road with jet.

text.p: Striking workers at the Craiova Avioane SA plane maker in southwest Romania, whose output was halted by the war in ex-Yugoslavia, used a jet fighter to block traffic near their city on Monday, local union leaders said.
"Starting this morning, some 2,000 workers went on strike and blocked traffic outside the plant," Ion Ionescu, deputy leader of the plant's trade union told Reuters by telephone from Craiova.

The protesters, he said, demanding job security, used a jet fighter produced at the plant to block traffic on the main E70 motorway, which links Bucharest to the western city of Timisoara on the Yugoslav border.
They wanted executives of the state-owned plant to ensure orders and relaunch production and to guarantee jobs for its staff, which fell to 2,700 employees down from 4,700 in 1992.

Monday's stoppage was launched after plant managers refused to extend by another month a government scheme giving arms industry workers 75 percent pay for 180 days a year in the absence of orders, Ionescu said.
"People are scared, they fear they might lose their jobs. I really don't know how this situation will develop," he said.

The Craiova plant was built in the 1970s with an initial investment of $100 million, part of a joint Romanian-Yugoslav project to build 200 IAR 93-Orao sub-sonic jet fighter-bombers for the air forces of the two neighbouring Balkan states.
But previous trade sanctions imposed by the United Nations on former Yugoslavia over its role in the Bosnian war brought the plant, 250 km (150 miles) west of Bucharest, to a virtual standstill.
Ionescu said the only orders at the plant were to do simple repairs of the IAR93s used by the Romanian air force.
